speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You presented with fever and altered mentation for two days; to begin our assessment, have you had any recent head trauma, seizures, or loss of consciousness?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of tics and current use of haloperidol, have you noticed any new muscle stiffness, difficulty swallowing, or a change in the way you move since starting this medication?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS) caused by haloperidol toxicity.
